excerpts.content:
I think out of all the tweets I quickly scanned, Marius' tweet drove the point clearly and succintly regarding the need for both nodes.

In general a few areas I think can be done:
1. A Centralized point of guide for everyone. (I think these already exists and sufficient to some extent). Bonus if there's just a quick checklist for people to check with depending on their needs, e.g. if u're a staker, u need x,y,z,etc

2. A  socialization campaign across social media. (Not just through EF official account but also maybe through some coredevs with large following, and you too Tim!) I would like to see it also on reddit and crypto centric subreddits and even ethmining subreddit if possible.

3. Sustained call to action - we need to remind people consistently so if we're doing it through social media, we probably need people to repost things consistently for quite a while

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: One gap  in the merge-readiness checklist is that it's just that, a checklist. It doesn't say how to do those things, just to do them. The mechanisms will vary by client  -- that's why something like the Kiln (or soon Goerli) launchpad information is so useful, it's a specific/concise way of documenting what some of the basic important flags for the merge are (JWT, engine API, etc) across clients

excerpts.author: sharkhuh
excerpts.content: I read somewhere that Goerli is PoA? What does that mean exactly when comparing it to PoW?

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: the main difference is that there is a fixed, known set of block producers compared to PoW so you end up with much less uncertainty around when blocks will arrive — and consequently have a better idea around difficulty and difficulty estimation

excerpts.content: no work component, it’s more like a permissioned proof of stake
